title: Latency Underlay Splitter: percentile underlay + stream-shadow panels by model/route
creator: Maya Singh
description: Build a new dashboard experience that shows p50/p95/p99 percentile underlays for each model-route with an explicit streaming vs non-streaming 'shadow' overlay. Goal: make anomalous percentile divergence and stream/non-stream splits immediately discoverable and linkable to traces. This ticket covers backend metric query changes, minor schema additions to the metrics pipeline to tag stream-mode vs blocking-mode consistently, dashboard panel design and rollout, and trace-link plumbing from percentile spikes to sampled traces. This work is targeted to reduce mean time to root cause when customers observe high tail latency in production and to provide visibility needed for runtime tuning recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard page accessible under Console -> Observability -> Latency Underlay
Per-model/route panels show p50/p95/p99 lines and an underlay heat region representing distribution density
Streaming vs non-streaming toggle that overlays 'stream shadow' (semi-transparent) showing separate percentiles and counts
Each percentile spike point has a direct link that opens a trace search with pre-filled filters (model, route, request_shape, stream_flag)
Backend query cost remains within 1.5x of current latency panels for 30m windows by using precomputed rollups and sampling heuristics
Rollout plan includes canary to 10% of orgs and a fallback route to previous dashboard if query error rate > 2%
Docs and runbook updated: README for panel metrics, query patterns, and alert thresholds
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after observability guild sync. Identified need to separate stream-mode telemetry which is currently inconsistently labeled in the pipeline.
2025-02-21: Spike completed—confirmed existing metrics pipeline lacks a stable stream_flag. Patch proposed to metrics-enricher to add deterministic 'io_mode' tag (values: streaming, blocking).
2025-02-25: Backend first-pass: added rollup tables for percentile sketches per (model, route, io_mode, minute) — PR opened: github.com/redwood/metrics/pulls/4521
2025-02-28: Design review with Console UX. Agreed on underlay + shadow pattern; provided mockups in Drive: drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/obs-latency-underlay-mocks
2025-03-03: Instrumented trace-link scheme; traces now accept query params model,route,io_mode,request_shape. Integration test added to trace-service harness.

2025-03-05: Performance profiling shows rollup read path adds ~20ms median to panel render on a standard org; optimizing query fanout next. Blocking: need final approval from infra on rollup storage cost (ticketed to FIN-ops).
notes: Implementation choices considered: (1) compute percentiles on the fly from raw metrics (accurate but expensive), (2) maintain t-digest rollups per minute (chosen for cost/accuracy tradeoff), (3) use sampled k-v cache traces to link to spike points (used for trace linkage).
UX trade-offs: underlay shows density which can be noisy for low-traffic routes; we will default to hide underlay under low-volume threshold and surface a tooltip explaining sample size.
Follow-ups: instrumentation audit to ensure third-party models (customer-provided) have correct io_mode tagging; create regression tests to prevent tag erosion.
On-call runbook draft: if dashboard query errors exceed 2% or latency read path > 500ms, rollback via console feature flag and open ENG rollback ticket.
